source_text: Descent of finiteness properties of modules

<STRUCT_0001>
This section is the analogue for the case of algebraic spaces of
Descent, Section <REF_0001>.
The goal is to show that one can check a quasi-coherent module
has a certain finiteness conditions by checking on the members of
a covering. We will repeatedly use the following proof scheme.
Suppose that <MATH_0001> is an algebraic space, and that <MATH_0002>
is a fppf (resp.<SPACE_0001>fpqc) covering. Let <MATH_0003> be a surjective
<ACCENT_0001>tale morphism such that <MATH_0004> is a scheme. Then there exists an
fppf (resp.<SPACE_0002>fpqc) covering <MATH_0005> such that
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0006> is a refinement of <MATH_0007>,
<STRUCT_0004> each <MATH_0008> is a scheme, and
<STRUCT_0005> each morphism <MATH_0009> factors though <MATH_0010>, and
<STRUCT_0006> <MATH_0011> is an fppf (resp.<SPACE_0003>fpqc) covering of <MATH_0012>.
<STRUCT_0007>
Namely, first refine <MATH_0013> by an fppf (resp.<SPACE_0004>fpqc)
covering such that each <MATH_0014> is a scheme, see
Topologies on Spaces, Lemma <REF_0002>,
resp.<SPACE_0005>Lemma <REF_0003>.
Then set <MATH_0015>. A quasi-coherent
<MATH_0016>-module <MATH_0017> is of finite type, of
finite presentation, etc if and only if the quasi-coherent
<MATH_0018>-module <MATH_0019> is of finite type, of
finite presentation, etc. Hence we can use the existence of the
refinement <MATH_0020> to reduce the proof of the following
lemmas to the case of schemes. We will indicate this by saying
that ``<TEXTITOPEN_0001>the result follows from the case of schemes by
<ACCENT_0002>tale localization<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>''.
